_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Lymm
suggestions.editorialDescription: A medieval cross at the crossroads, a duck pond that's outlasted every plan to modernise around it, and a run of independent shops and canalside pubs that never quite gave in to Altrincham's gravity a few miles up the road.
suggestions.researchNotes: Found via this run's required per-day new-district check, not user-named — a genuine gap surfaced while researching venues, not manufactured to fill the check. Lymm is a well-known, distinct Cheshire village on the Bridgewater Canal, consistently described (Great British Life, visitcheshire.com, roam-local.co.uk) as one of Cheshire's most desirable villages, with a real independent-shop cluster around the historic Lymm Cross (Xross Interiors, Bird and Bay, Watson and Wilde, Collect Art) and named, non-chain dining (Eighteen The Cross wine bar and restaurant). Passes the 'would a local raise an eyebrow this isn't already covered' test the same way Prestbury/Knutsford/Cheadle Hulme did. Notably, this file's own venues.json already has two real venues seeded under the 'altrincham' district purely by proximity-of-convenience — Lymm Golf Club and Lymm Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club — because no Lymm district has existed until now, the same 'real location, no home district yet' situation Wilmslow Golf Club (seeded in Mobberley) and Beeston Castle (seeded in Tarporley) already established precedent for; if this district is promoted, those two venues would be natural (but not decided-here) candidates to re-home. Coordinates (53.38105, -2.47763) are Lymm town centre / Lymm Cross, independently verified via web search rather than invented. Distance check: roughly 8.5km (5.3 miles) from the existing Altrincham district centroid — clearly distinct, comfortably past the separation already accepted for other close Cheshire pairs (Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme ~2 miles, Tarporley/Northwich corridor). accentColor (#6C8A93, a soft canal-water blue-teal) chosen for the real Bridgewater Canal character and checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing Cheshire accent, closest neighbours Macclesfield's verdigris (#4F6B63) and Northwich's river-slate-teal (#4A6B6E) — both notably darker/greener than this lighter, more blue-grey tone. base (50) is a reasoned estimate, similar register to Alderley Edge (52) and just below Knutsford (54) — a genuinely desirable village with real everyday commercial life, not a bustling town centre. Not added to the Golden Triangle group — that group's canonical definition (Alderley Edge/Prestbury/Wilmslow, sometimes Knutsford/Mobberley) doesn't include Lymm in any source checked. No venues suggested for it in this same run — same 'district entry only, venues as separate follow-up work' precedent every prior district promotion has followed.

suggestions.name: Ramsbottom
suggestions.editorialDescription: A former cotton town in the Irwell valley, with the East Lancashire Railway's steam engines still terminating where the mills once ran — Bridge Street's chip shops and craft-gift windows give way at night to a food scene locals drive in for, not just visit on the way to the moors above it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Found via this run's required per-day new-district check, not user-named. Ramsbottom is a well-known former cotton-mill town in the Irwell valley (Metropolitan Borough of Bury, Greater Manchester), consistently name-checked in 'best food towns near Manchester' coverage (Manchester Confidential's own dedicated 'insider's guide to eating and drinking in Ramsbottom', Manchester's Finest's Bury/Ramsbottom guide) with a genuinely distinct, independent-heavy food and drink scene (Eagle & Child — voted best roast dinner in Greater Manchester; Colleen's; Owen's, overlooking the East Lancashire Railway station; a well-regarded Japanese specialist; independent cafes, bakeries and coffee shops) and a real, working heritage railway terminus (the East Lancashire Railway, reopened 1987) that no existing Manchester-metro district shares. Passes the 'would a local raise an eyebrow this isn't already covered' test the same way Prestbury/Knutsford/Cheadle Hulme did originally, and the same way this file's own precedent (Heaton Moor, Bramhall, Stockport Underbanks, Cheadle Hulme) already treats real Greater Manchester boroughs outside the City of Manchester itself as fair game under the same shorthand. Coordinates (53.64789, -2.31683) are Ramsbottom's real town-centre centroid, independently verified via web geocoding rather than invented; Bridge Street itself (the town's real commercial spine, home to several Grade II-listed 19th-century terraces per British Listed Buildings) sits within a few hundred metres of this point. Distance check: roughly 9.3 miles (15km) north of Manchester city centre and well clear of every existing Manchester-metro district (Heaton Moor, the nearest, sits well over 9 miles south) — clearly distinct, no overlap. accentColor (#7A6A5C, a warm weathered taupe-brown evoking millstone and moorland stone) chosen for perceptual distinctness against every existing Manchester-metro accent — closest neighbours Bramhall's heather-plum (#7D6B87, notably more purple) and Prestbury's walnut-brown (#6B4A3D, notably darker/redder) — distinct from both. base (64) is a reasoned estimate, similar register to Heaton Moor (68) and Chinatown (68) — a real, bustling small-town high street rather than a dense inner-city district. kind 'city', matching the pattern every other Manchester-metro district in this file already uses (the county/city split is specifically a Cheshire-only distinction per this file's own established convention). No district group added — Ramsbottom doesn't fit any existing group's real geography. No venues suggested for it in this same run — same 'district entry only, venues as separate follow-up work' precedent every prior district promotion has followed.
